facts.statement: He was born on 13 September 1865 at Kirkee, near Poona, in India, the second son of Herbert Mills Birdwood.
He was educated at Clifton College and the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, joined the 12th Lancers in India in 1885 and transferred to the 11th Bengal Lancers in 1887.
In 1894 he married Janetta Hope Gonville Bromhead, daughter of Sir Benjamin Parnell Bromhead, 4th Baronet.
He was appointed C.I.E. in 1908 and received the D.S.O. for the operations against the Zakka Khel and Mohmands, dated 18 July 1908.
In November 1914 Kitchener gave him command of the Australian and New Zealand troops gathering in Egypt.
His corps landed at Anzac on 25 April 1915, in the campaign commanded by General Sir Ian Hamilton.
He commanded I ANZAC Corps from 1916 and then the Australian Corps, which he handed to Sir John Monash on 31 May 1918, before taking command of the Fifth Army.
He was promoted field marshal in 1925 and was Commander-in-Chief in India from 1925 to 1930.
He was elected Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge, in 1931.
In 1938 he was created Baron Birdwood, of Anzac and of Totnes.
He published two volumes of recollections, Khaki and Gown and In My Time: Recollections and Anecdotes.
He died at Hampton Court Palace and was buried at Twickenham.

uncertainties.decision: The ADB gives 17 May 1951; Westminster Abbey gives 19 May 1951. The page names the year only.
The ADB gives 1946. The AETERNUS edition follows the Skeffington & Son first edition, dated to December 1945; a second edition followed in May 1946. The page says first published in 1945.
The ADB and The Complete Peerage give 1894; other references give 1893. The page follows 1894.
Foreign orders and decorations are listed by the year of their notice in the London or Edinburgh Gazette, not by the date of the foreign award.

interpretation.note: In My Time is read as an old soldier's book of anecdote and character, not as a record of his commands; no judgement of his generalship is offered beyond the sources.

en.tagline: The general the Anzacs called Birdie, and the old soldier who remembered them as comrades.
en.intro: William Riddell Birdwood came out of the cavalry of British India to lead the Australian and New Zealand troops ashore at Anzac in 1915. He stayed with them through Gallipoli and France, and ended his service as a field marshal and Commander-in-Chief in India.
en.orientation: Birdwood's career runs from the frontier regiments of the 1880s to the last years of the Raj. In between lies the command for which he is remembered: the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps, from its gathering in Egypt to the Western Front.
en.originHeading: Kirkee, Clifton and the Bengal Lancers
origin: He was born at Kirkee, near Poona, in 1865, the second son of Herbert Mills Birdwood. After Clifton College and Sandhurst he joined the 12th Lancers in India in 1885 and moved two years later to the 11th Bengal Lancers.
In 1894 he married Janetta Hope Gonville Bromhead. In 1908 he was appointed C.I.E., and the operations against the Zakka Khel and Mohmands brought him the D.S.O.
career: In November 1914 Kitchener gave him the Australian and New Zealand troops gathering in Egypt. His corps landed at Anzac on 25 April 1915, in the campaign commanded by Sir Ian Hamilton.

In France he commanded I ANZAC Corps and the Australian Corps, which he handed to Sir John Monash on 31 May 1918 before taking the Fifth Army. He was promoted field marshal in 1925 and was Commander-in-Chief in India until 1930. He then became Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge, and in 1938 a peer as Baron Birdwood, of Anzac and of Totnes. He died at Hampton Court Palace in 1951.
literature: He wrote two books of recollections, Khaki and Gown and In My Time: Recollections and Anecdotes, the second published by Skeffington & Son in London.
In My Time is not the record of his commands. It is a book of the men he served with: regimental characters, Indian officers, viceroys, Anzacs and Cambridge dons, remembered in anecdote.
en.legacy: The Anzacs called him Birdie. Thirty years after Gallipoli he still wrote of them as comrades, and that loyalty gives his last book its warmth.
en.bridge: In My Time: Recollections and Anecdotes, first published in London in 1945. An English AETERNUS edition in the Green Series is in preparation.
en.description: William Riddell Birdwood (1865–1951): Bengal Lancer, commander of the Anzacs at Gallipoli and in France, field marshal and Commander-in-Chief in India, with In My Time in preparation at AETERNUS.
